question.text: Gomati Opportunities AIF (Cat II) is updating its internal governance. Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, which of the following statements about fiduciary duty and conflicts is CORRECT?

answer.text: Sponsor has fiduciary duty; Manager has only contractual duties to investors

The Sponsor AND Manager/Trustee of an AIF have a FIDUCIARY DUTY towards investors; they are bound to disclose all conflicts of interest as and when they arise or are likely to arise; every AIF shall have a CONFLICT OF INTEREST POLICY
Fiduciary duty applies only if the AIF is structured as a trust, not as an LLP or company
Conflict disclosure is required only at the time of annual PPM update

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter, 'The Sponsor and Manager/Trustee of an AIF have a fiduciary duty towards investors in the fund. They are bound to disclose all conflicts of interests as and when they arise or are likely to arise. Every AIF shall have a Conflict of Interest Policy, which helps to identify and mitigate the potential conflicts. Managers and Sponsors have the responsibility to monitor the compliance towards the conflict of interest policy.' The Trap: The Sponsor-only option narrowly limits fiduciary duty. The trust-only option wrongly limits by legal form (fiduciary duty applies across trust/LLP/company structures). The annual-only option delays disclosure timing (it must be AS AND WHEN conflicts arise, not annually). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same fiduciary framework. X-A/X-B tests IA fiduciary standard. XV tests Research Analyst conflicts. Fiduciary concept is a SEBI-wide theme across intermediary regs. Manager's Pro-Tip: Operationalise the Conflict Policy with a Conflicts Register — log every identified/potential conflict with date, nature, disclosure steps, resolution. SEBI inspectors will ask for this register in any AIF-focused inspection. Review quarterly at the IC.
